title: Research Scientist – Molecular Diagnostics
description:
Our Bosch Research team occupies a critical position between academic research and product development, distinguishing us from many other companies. We engage with academia, incubate ideas, advance them to the prototype stage, and collaborate with development teams in our business units to support product development based on our research outcomes. We are seeking a research scientist with a strong academic background, proven industry experience, and a passion for tackling complex, real-world problems in molecular diagnostics.
Our R&D center is located in Sunnyvale, CA, USA. This is in the heart of Silicon Valley in close proximity to Stanford University and UC Berkeley. The candidate will be a key contributor to our research and development efforts, from conceptualization to the creation of novel technologies. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with industry experience who is eager to make a significant impact in the field of molecular sensors and biotechnology.
Responsibilities:
• Identify, incubate, and translate cutting-edge academic research into functional, scalable proof-of-concept technologies in molecular diagnostics and biosensing.
• Lead hands-on development and testing of prototype diagnostic systems, integrating microfluidics, electrochemical sensing, soft electronics, and chip-scale nanofabrication.
• Collaborate closely with internal business units, engineering teams, and external academic partners (e.g., Stanford, UC Berkeley) to transition early-stage research into commercially viable product pipelines.
• Design and execute advanced experiments for single-molecule detection, assay integration, and sample-to-answer cartridge performance.
• Protect innovation through patent filings while contributing high-impact scientific publications and technical documentation.
• Serve as a subject matter expert in biosensors and bioelectronics, advising multidisciplinary teams on technical feasibility, risk mitigation, and system architecture.
• Education: PhD in a relevant field (e.g., Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Bioengineering, Physics, or a related discipline)
• Industry Experience: 3-5 years of previous industry experience in a relevant biotechnology company. We highly value experience in translating academic ideas into real-world products.
• Molecular Diagnostics Expertise: Proven experience in building real-world solutions in the biotechnology sector, particularly in single molecule detection and instrumentation for molecular diagnostics.
• Integrated Systems Experience: Demonstrated experience with integrated molecular diagnostic platforms, such as cartridge design, on-chip sample-prep, and electronics.
• Soft Electronics: experience with soft electronics for applications in biosensing.
• Micro/Nanofabrication: experience with chip design and process development for applications in biosensing.
• Electrochemical Sensing: experience with electrochemical systems and biosensors.
• Biochemistry: familiarity with the principles of biochemistry.
• Proven track record of scientific accomplishment/patent filings
• Soft skills: highly motivated and passionate about developing new technologies and products; strong documentation, oral and interpersonal skills, experience working in a multidisciplinary team.
This is a U.S. based position, domestic relocation and local sponsorship considered on a per candidate basis.
The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $150,000 - $170,000. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, job location, etc. Your Recruiter can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process.
In addition to your base salary, Bosch offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision plans; health savings accounts (HSA); flexible spending accounts; 401(K) retirement plans with an employer match; wellness programs; life insurance; short- and long-term disability insurance; paid time off; parental leave, adoption assistance; and reimbursement of education expenses.
Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans.
*Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date.

Our team builds machine learning models for some of the largest health plans in the country to identify and audit claims errors from simple errors to outright fraud. Our claim selection models help with selecting the right set of claims to audit and recover hundreds of millions of dollars each year reducing wasted medical spend. title: AI Solution Engineer
description:
## AI Solution Engineer
## Work Type: Part-time.
Schedule: U.S. business hours (CST preferred).
## Location: 100% Remote.
## About the Role
We are looking for an AI Automation & Integration Engineer to maintain, optimize, and expand our existing automation ecosystem while developing new AI-powered features and intelligent workflows.
The company currently operates on an interconnected technology stack that includes Trello, a custom-built in-house CRM, Jotform, Zapier, and Make. The initial priority for this role will be to understand how these systems work together, troubleshoot existing integrations, identify inefficiencies, and improve the reliability of our current workflows.
Beyond maintenance, this person will help build the next generation of our internal operations by transforming manual, multi-step business processes into intelligent workflows powered by AI agents and automation. The goal is to create systems where agents can execute tasks, coordinate information, interact with external tools, and escalate decisions to humans when necessary.
This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who can work independently, understand inherited systems, make sound architectural decisions, and take AI-powered solutions from concept to production.
## Key Responsibilities
## 1. Automation Debugging & System Maintenance
Take ownership of existing automations and integrations across Trello, the custom CRM, Jotform, Zapier, and Make.
Diagnose workflow failures, identify root causes, and implement sustainable fixes rather than temporary workarounds.
Evaluate existing automation architecture and identify opportunities to improve performance, reliability, and maintainability.
Recommend whether existing workflows should be optimized, repaired, or rebuilt.
## 2. Systems Integration & API Development
Build and maintain integrations between project management, CRM, form platforms, and external applications.
Work with REST APIs, webhooks, authentication mechanisms, rate limits, retries, and data mapping.
Analyze undocumented or custom-built systems by reviewing schemas, existing implementations, and available technical resources.
Ensure accurate and consistent data synchronization across connected platforms.
## 3. AI Agents & Context Engineering
Develop AI-powered agents capable of executing multi-step business processes with minimal human intervention.
Implement context retrieval, memory management, conversation state, and relevant information injection.
Optimize context windows and retrieval strategies to maintain accuracy and consistency across complex workflows.
Design human-in-the-loop mechanisms for reviewing outputs, approving sensitive actions, and escalating exceptions.
## 4. Workflow Automation & Orchestration
Audit, maintain, rebuild, and extend workflows using Zapier and Make.
Leverage n8n or comparable orchestration platforms when they provide a more effective solution.
Coordinate AI models, APIs, external tools, and business logic across multi-step workflows.
Design task decomposition, execution sequences, dependencies, error handling, and recovery mechanisms.
## 5. AI Feature Development
Build new internal tools, integrations, and automation features that support business operations.
Develop maintainable solutions using Python, TypeScript, or comparable programming languages.
Integrate LLMs and third-party APIs based on performance, reliability, complexity, and cost considerations.
Translate operational requirements into practical technical solutions.
## 6. Testing, Evaluation & Optimization
Test AI agents against representative business scenarios and measurable performance criteria.
Identify failure patterns and improve accuracy, consistency, response times, and overall reliability.
Validate structured outputs, tool calling, and automated decision-making.
Continuously refine prompts, workflows, and agent behavior based on real-world performance.
## 7. Deployment & Production Monitoring
Take solutions from prototype through testing, deployment, and ongoing optimization.
Monitor production workflows, troubleshoot failures, and implement safeguards.
Maintain version control, technical documentation, and code quality standards.
Apply appropriate security practices when handling credentials, API keys, and sensitive business information.
## 8. Continuous Technical Improvement
Stay current with emerging AI models, agent frameworks, orchestration tools, and context engineering practices.
Evaluate new technologies and determine their practical value for the company's existing infrastructure.
Identify opportunities to replace repetitive manual processes with reliable, AI-assisted workflows.
## Required Qualifications & Technical Skills
Professional Experience:3–5 years of professional software engineering experience, including maintaining, debugging, and extending systems originally developed by other engineers.
AI & Intelligent Automation:Hands-on experience building AI-powered applications, intelligent automations, or agent-based workflows.
Debugging & Troubleshooting:Proven ability to take ownership of inherited automations, trace failures across interconnected platforms, and explain technical issues and their root causes.
Systems Integration:Experience integrating CRM, project management, and form platforms through REST APIs, webhooks, and custom integrations.
Programming:Strong proficiency in Python or TypeScript, including writing maintainable code and troubleshooting complex application issues.
Databases & Data Modeling: Experience with SQL, database structures, data modeling, and designing reliable data synchronization between systems.
Workflow Automation:Practical, hands-on experience with both Zapier and Make is required.
LLM Integration:Experience integrating LLM provider APIs, structured outputs, tool calling, and prompt engineering into real-world applications.
Context Engineering:Understanding of memory management, retrieval, conversation state, and context optimization for multi-step AI workflows.
Software Engineering Practices: Familiarity with Git, GitHub, API design, testing, debugging, and collaborative development.
Architecture & Technical Judgment:Ability to evaluate existing systems, identify inefficiencies, and determine when to optimize, repair, or rebuild.
Production Experience:Ability to take solutions from initial development through testing, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement.
Security Awareness:Understanding of secure credential management, API key protection, least-privilege access, and responsible handling of sensitive information.
Autonomy: Comfortable making technical decisions, prioritizing competing requirements, and delivering results with limited supervision.
## Communication & Problem-Solving Skills
Strong written English communication skills. C1 or High.
Ability to conduct technical discovery and ask the right questions before proposing or developing solutions.
Comfortable translating operational challenges into technical requirements and practical implementation plans.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, particularly when working with undocumented or inherited systems.
Understands when AI-generated outputs require human verification, approval, or escalation.
Able to communicate technical limitations, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations to non-technical stakeholders.
Self-directed, accountable, and proactive in following up on blockers and pending decisions.
## Nice-to-Have Qualifications

Experience administering or integrating custom-built CRM platforms.
Familiarity with agent frameworks and orchestration libraries such as LangGraph and LangChain.
Experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP) and connecting AI agents to external services.

Experience with AI evaluation frameworks, observability, tracing, guardrails, and automated testing.

Für neue Interessenten bist du die erste Ansprechperson bei elunic und zeigst ihnen, was ein eluna-Agent in ihren Abläufen im Büro erledigt. Nach dem ersten Abschluss gibst du an unsere AI Sales Consultants ab, mit wachsender Erfahrung betreust du deine Kunden später selbst weiter. Du arbeitest remote.
## Was du tatsächlich tust
Du findest und qualifizierst neue Kunden. Zielkunden und Entscheider recherchierst du selbst, etwa über LinkedIn und HubSpot. Vom Erstkontakt bis zur ersten Websession bist du ihr Gegenüber.
Du zeigst eluna am konkreten Fall. In Demo-Terminen spielst du durch, was ein Agent beim Kunden erledigt, zum Beispiel eine Service-Anfrage, eine Ersatzteilbestellung oder ein Angebot. Dabei übersetzt du die Technik in Nutzen für sein Team.
Du holst den ersten Abschluss und gibst dann ab. Danach übernimmt unser AI Sales Consulting. Deine Empfehlungen für weitere Anwendungsfälle sind die Grundlage für die weitere Kundenentwicklung.
Ein Ergebnis aus einem Kundenprojekt: Eine Service-Anfrage braucht jetzt 45 Sekunden, vorher waren es 25 Minuten. Bei Ausnahmen entscheidet ein Mensch.
## Das bist du
Du hast schon etwas angestoßen und zu Ende gebracht. Ein Kundensegment, ein Prozess, ein eigenes Projekt, auch gegen Widerstände. Welche Station, ist uns weniger wichtig als das Muster.
Du findest auf jeder Ebene den passenden Ton. Ob Maschinenbedienerin oder Werkleiter, du wechselst ohne Mühe zwischen den Ebenen.
Du verstehst, warum KI einen Unterschied macht. Programmieren musst du nicht. Wie KI-Lösungen funktionieren, weißt du schon oder eignest es dir schnell an.
Was du wirklich brauchst: Deutsch auf verhandlungssicherem Niveau, weil du mit Kunden im Termin sitzt.
Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Informatikstudium, Berufsjahre oder Erfahrung in der Industrie setzen wir nicht voraus. Das Industriewissen lernst du bei uns.

Wir arbeiten KI-first, in allen Rollen. KI nimmt dir Routine ab, der Anspruch an deine Arbeit steigt dadurch. Damit alle mitkommen, steht Lernzeit fest im Kalender.
Deine Kunden suchst du dir selbst. Recherche und Erstkontakt gehören genauso zur Rolle wie Demos. Unklare Situationen und wechselnde Prioritäten sind Teil des Jobs.
Ehrlich gesagt passen wir eher nicht zusammen, wenn du feste Vorgaben von außen brauchst oder KI für ein Thema für später hältst.
## Was du bekommst
KI-Werkzeuge ohne Formular, dazu unsere eigenen Agenten. Neue Modelle probierst du direkt im Projekt aus.

9 Stunden Lernzeit pro Woche und bis zu 600 € im Jahr für Kurse und Konferenzen.
Dein Rhythmus: Teilzeit und Elternzeit möglich, Arbeitszeiten flexibel.
Dazu: EGYM Wellpass, Jobrad, Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket, Teamevents und Workations.

Kein Anschreiben, Lebenslauf oder LinkedIn-Profil reicht. Am meisten freut uns ein Link auf etwas, das du gebaut hast. KI darfst du dabei nutzen.
Video-Interview. Ein paar kurze Fragen, wann es dir passt.
Kennenlern-Call. Über dich, die Rolle und deine Fragen.
Gespräch mit einem Gründer. Wohin elunic will, aus erster Hand.
Use Case. Eine echte Aufgabe, mit den Werkzeugen aus dem Job.
Unsicher, ob es passt? Mach den AI Harness-Check oder lass deinen eigenen Agenten prüfen, ob wir zu dir passen.
Über elunic. Wir bringen KI in den industriellen Mittelstand, mit rund 60 Leuten im Kernteam und einem festen Netz aus Partnern. Mit eluna bauen wir KI-Agenten, die im Büro unserer Kunden Vorgänge erledigen, von der Service-Anfrage bis zum Angebot.

description:
## ABOUT UNRAVEL CARBON
Unravel Carbon is an enterprise software that helps companies track and reduce their carbon emissions, focusing on Asia, based in Singapore.
It is the first AI-powered decarbonization platform in Asia that converts any company's accounting data into full supply chain carbon data in seconds, generates climate solutions automatically and auto-populates regulatory disclosure reports.
We aim to accelerate the participation of all companies, big and small, in the global fight against climate change. And we want to do it the 21st century way—autonomous, painless, and beautiful.
Unravel consists of a team of software engineers, data scientists, founders and climate experts with a passion to solve the world's most pressing issue—climate change. Collectively, our leadership team has launched and invested in multiple companies, and are now combining their experience and knowledge here at Unravel.
We are backed by some of the world's best funds and investors such as Y Combinator, Sequoia.
Unravel was founded in Q4/2021 with headquarters in Singapore.
## ABOUT THE ROLE
We are hiring a full-stack Software Engineer in Japan to help build Unravel Carbon's product for a growing base of customers across Asia and beyond. This is a hands-on, full-stack engineering role: you will work across the data layer, backend and frontend, lead projects end to end on our product roadmap, solve hard problems across the platform and ship production code.
Japan is one of our key markets. description:
Cheesecake Labs é parceira de IA, dados e engenharia de produto para organizações consolidadas e em fase de escala que enfrentam sistemas legados, dados fragmentados, pressão por IA ou capacidade de engenharia limitada.
Nossos serviços incluem Implementação de IA, Modernização de Aplicações, Data & Analytics, Product Engineering, Entrega Acelerada por IA e Times de Engenharia Integrados. Entregamos workflows agênticos em 8 a 12 semanas e modernizamos aplicações em 5 a 10 meses, em vez de 2 anos. Também construímos bases de dados confiáveis e produtos digitais feitos para escalar. Nosso ciclo de desenvolvimento de software agêntico acelera a execução, enquanto engenheiros experientes se integram aos times dos clientes para trazer profundidade técnica, segurança e clareza de ownership.
Membro do Claude Partner Network da Anthropic. Entre nossos parceiros de tecnologia estão Databricks, Snowflake, dbt e AWS.
Em mais de 13 anos, a Cheesecake Labs construiu mais de 300 produtos para clientes como Eurasia Group, MoneyGram, World Bank, Stellar, Wedgewood, PepsiCo, Merck, Sodexo e Mercado Libre.
## Detalhes da contratação
• Modelo de contractor, por projeto
• Pagamento em USD por hora
• 100% remoto
• Alocação flexível, conforme a disponibilidade de projetos e o fit
• As oportunidades podem variar em duração, escopo e dedicação semanal, de acordo com as necessidades dos clientes
Algumas oportunidades podem começar imediatamente.
Outras podem ser ativadas conforme novos projetos entrarem no nosso pipeline.
## A história por trás desta vaga
Muitas vagas de engenharia de IA ainda giram em torno de experimentos, protótipos isolados ou pesquisa. Esta não é uma delas.
Na Cheesecake Labs, construímos software e soluções com IA para empresas reais, com usuários reais, restrições reais e prazos reais. Nossos squads são pequenos e seniores, e entregam em semanas e meses, não em anos.
Hoje, agentes de IA escrevem a maior parte do nosso código. Esta vaga é para quem decide como as coisas são construídas, direciona os agentes, verifica o resultado e responde por ele diante do cliente.
Estamos buscando uma pessoa Engenheira de Software Sênior: alguém que assume um projeto de cliente desde a primeira conversa de escopo até a produção, e que lida com as decisões de negócio, produto e técnica no caminho. Quando o projeto tem PM, a direção de produto fica com essa pessoa e você é a contraparte técnica dela. Quando não tem, você recebe o problema direto do founder ou do cliente.
## Como é esta vaga na prática
Esta não é uma vaga de “receber tickets e implementar features”. Também não é uma vaga de “escrever cada linha na mão”.
## Em um projeto típico, você pode:
• Rodar o nosso Spec Driven, nosso fluxo de desenvolvimento orientado a specs: reunir contexto, especificar, planejar, implementar por meio de agentes de IA, revisar e fechar o ciclo.
• Transformar um problema de negócio do cliente em um desenho técnico e em uma spec que um agente de IA consiga executar e que você consiga verificar.
• Trabalhar com PM, designer e o squad para entender o que deve ser construído, ou receber os requisitos direto do founder ou do cliente quando não há PM.
• Participar de conversas com o cliente sobre objetivos, escopo e trade-offs técnicos, e mantê-lo atualizado por escrito ao longo do caminho.
• Direcionar agentes de IA (Claude Code, Cursor ou similares) para implementar a partir da sua spec. Escrever código à mão é a exceção, não o padrão.
• Revisar o que os agentes produzem, combinando loops automatizados de revisão com a sua própria checagem de arquitetura e comportamento, e responder por 100% do que é entregue.
• Tomar as decisões de arquitetura. A IA executa, você decide.
• Entregar e iterar, e depois fechar o ciclo devolvendo decisões e edge cases ao contexto do projeto, para que a próxima spec comece mais bem informada.
• Usar todos os dias o nosso harness compartilhado (skills, agentes e loops de revisão), melhorá-lo e devolver o que funciona, para que todos os squads se beneficiem.
• Trabalhar dentro das regras de cada cliente sobre o uso de IA (veja Como usamos IA aqui).
Alguns projetos pesam mais na arquitetura. Outros, nas conversas com o cliente. A maioria mistura os dois. Você trabalha com bastante autonomia, e conta com um Engineering Manager e com o squad quando precisar.
## O que costuma funcionar bem por aqui
## Quem se destaca nesta vaga costuma:
• Ter construído e entregue produtos de software reais de ponta a ponta, com JS/Typescript, e/ou Python, e conseguir explicar as decisões que tomou.
• Já usar agentes de IA todos os dias para projetar, construir, depurar e pesquisar, e conseguir mostrar o que construiu.
• Pensar em specs: transformar ambiguidade em definições estruturadas e testáveis.
• Ter mentalidade full-stack. Backend, frontend, IA ou produto podem ser o seu forte, e você circula entre as camadas quando o projeto precisa.
• Verificar antes de dizer “pronto” e deixar claro o que foi e o que não foi verificado.
• Trazer problemas cedo, já com opções, e compartilhar o que aprendeu com o time.
• Atuar bem com alta autonomia, pouca burocracia e ciclos rápidos de feedback, em um formato 100% remoto.
## Talvez esta vaga não seja para você se
## Só para ser transparente:
• Você precisa de requisitos detalhados ou de direção constante antes de começar.
• Você vê a IA como ferramenta de apoio, ou prefere escrever a maior parte do código à mão.
• Você se sente confortável entregando resultado de IA que não verificou.
• Você prefere funções focadas só em implementação, sem conversa com cliente ou com o negócio.
• Você não se sente à vontade conversando direto com clientes ou lidando com problemas ambíguos.
• Você tende a ficar em silêncio entre o kickoff e a entrega.
• Você prefere prioridades estáveis a iteração rápida e alta ownership.
Não há nada de errado em nenhuma dessas preferências. Só não é assim que a gente trabalha.
## Uma última coisa
Para participar deste processo seletivo, você precisa:
• Ter um registro empresarial válido no seu país (CNPJ, VAT, EIN ou equivalente).
• Ter uma conta bancária apta a receber pagamentos em dólar (USD).
• Poder emitir invoices (notas fiscais ou equivalente) conforme necessário.
Esses requisitos são necessários para a contratação como prestador de serviços (contractor) e para o processamento dos pagamentos.
## Não tem certeza se atende a todos os requisitos?
## Tudo bem.
Sabemos que muitas pessoas excelentes, principalmente de grupos sub-representados, hesitam em se candidatar quando não atendem a 100% dos requisitos. Se esta oportunidade te interessa, queremos te conhecer mesmo assim.
DICA IMPORTANTE: a comunicação durante o processo seletivo é feita por e-mail. Sugerimos que você fique de olho na sua caixa de entrada e libere o recebimento de mensagens de @cheesecakelabs.hire.trakstar.com, para que nossas mensagens não caiam no spam ;)
## Como usamos IA aqui
Na Cheesecake Labs, agentes de IA fazem a maior parte da execução: código, infraestrutura, modelos de dados, pesquisa, protótipos e documentação. As pessoas tomam as decisões: o que será construído e em que ordem, a arquitetura, a alocação dos times e qualquer assunto que envolva pessoas. Todas as vagas aqui especificam, direcionam a IA, verificam o resultado e respondem pelo que é entregue.
Em todos os projetos, também seguimos algumas regras:
• Usar apenas ferramentas aprovadas, por meio das contas corporativas da Cheesecake Labs.
• Seguir as regras de cada cliente sobre IA. Alguns clientes exigem uma stack de IA específica, e mercados altamente regulados (como o setor bancário no Brasil) podem exigir modelos hospedados no país.
• Nunca inserir dados de clientes ou dados pessoais (nomes, datas de nascimento, e-mails) em uma LLM sem antes anonimizá-los. O mesmo vale para os dados das nossas próprias pessoas.
• Cumprir a LGPD e as demais leis de proteção de dados aplicáveis.
Os dados pessoais coletados serão usados apenas para gerenciar e controlar os currículos das pessoas candidatas, a fim de avaliar os requisitos necessários, como as informações de contato, e também para conduzir este processo seletivo.
Os dados coletados não serão compartilhados com terceiros sem a sua autorização, e seu uso será restrito à equipe interna da Cheesecake Labs e aos prestadores de serviço que processam seus dados para o processo seletivo. A qualquer momento, você pode entrar em contato conosco e removeremos seus dados do nosso sistema de coleta de dados. Para isso, basta enviar um e-mail para .

This Opportunity
Snowplow is rebuilding how the company runs its own work, and the Applied AI team owns Firn, the data and AI platform that work runs on, and the engineering standards that go with it. This role is an Applied AI engineer embedded with one business team, the way a site reliability engineer sits inside a product team: your line manager, your code reviewers and your career path come from Applied AI; your backlog and your day come from the team you serve. The Senior Director you report to still ships code.
Your team is Growth, the group inside Marketing that books new meetings for our sellers. Its workflows already produce pipeline: an always-on outbound engine that scores accounts daily and sends hundreds of personalized sequences, a campaign builder that turns an AE's target list into a reviewed campaign, a morning routine that ranks warm contacts by intent signal, enrichment and signal pipelines from Apollo, Vector, Kettlepoint and reo.dev into Snowflake, and a paid-media loop that adjusts ads. They were built by people close to the work to get results fast, and they did. Now they need an engineer who makes them production grade and keeps them improving.
You take over that estate, make it reliable, and make it better every week. The Director of Growth sets what matters, which is what moves pipeline now. You decide how it gets built and you build it. You work with our data engineers on scoring models and the semantic layer, with the platform engineer on the framework your workflows move onto, and with the Growth Associates and AEs who use what you ship. The engineering standards are Applied AI's; the tempo is Growth's.
What you will own
• The GTM workflows in production. The outbound orchestrator and its sequences, the campaign builder, the intent-signal routine, the enrichment and signal pipelines, and the paid-media loop. You know how each one runs, what it costs, and what to do when it breaks.
• Review steps before anything sends. Agents that check the list, confirm each signal is current, and review the copy before a sequence goes out, with a holdback gate and sampled human sign-off on anything headed for an inbox we have not already had a reply from.
• The learning loop. Replies and meetings booked feed back into who we contact and what we say. You instrument the sends, run A/B tests on variants, and show the Growth team which messaging is working.
• Signals and enrichment. The pipelines that bring third-party signals and first-party behavior into Snowflake: Kettlepoint job-change and hiring signals, Apollo firmographics, and our own event data. You also own the fields the Growth team needs exposed through our MCP tools, and the work with our data engineers that gets them there.
• Skills and routines for sellers. The Claude skills the Growth Associates and AEs run each morning, the campaign tooling, and the short working sessions that get a new team using them.
• Deliverability and suppression. One set of contact rules every sender reads, warm-inbox discipline, and the suppression windows that keep us welcome in people's inboxes.
• Engineering standards on your estate. Version control, alerting, tracing, runbooks and documented handover for every workflow you run, and a steady move of those workflows onto the Firn factory framework.
• The weekly cadence. A standing backlog with the Director of Growth, priorities set by pipeline, and a short written account of what shipped and what it did. When a priority and an engineering standard conflict, the Director of Growth and the Senior Director of Applied AI settle it together.
We would love to hear from you if you have
• Written software that runs in production. Python and SQL are your working languages, you use git every day, and when you meet a new API you read the docs and use it. Tools like n8n, Clay or Zapier are in your kit, and when they run out you write the code.
• Built with LLMs for real work. Prompts, tools, structured outputs and evaluation, and the failure modes of each. You know what a model does when a prompt does not say where to get its data, and you design against it.
• Run something that could not go down. Alerting, error handling, retries and recovery are habits, and when something does fail you fix the class of problem, not the instance.
• Moved data into a warehouse. You have built or maintained pipelines into Snowflake or an equivalent, and you can model a table in dbt or learn to quickly.
• Sat with sellers and marketers. You can take a growth director's ask, work out what they need, and come back with something they use the next week. When an ask is a symptom of a broken process, you say so before you build it.
• A fast tempo. The team you serve measures in meetings booked per week. You are measured on what you build: whether it runs, what it costs, and what it changed for the team. You ship small, measure, and say plainly when something is not working.
• An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, automation or agent you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process.
• Comfort being embedded. You can sit inside another team, take its priorities, and still hold the engineering standards your own team sets.
Bonus points for
• Experience with Salesforce, Apollo, Smartlead, Lemlist or similar GTM tooling and their APIs.
• Experience with email deliverability at volume.
• Experience with paid-media platform APIs.
How we hire for this role
The interview process includes a short technical exercise in code and a working session where you walk us through how you work with AI on a real task, using your own setup. We work this way ourselves, and you are welcome to use AI when applying.

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Reactivity use cases are at the heart of Loft's vision, and we are scaling them: from single-satellite reactive loops, to two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue (a detection from one sensor automatically cueing an acquisition by another), and ultimately multi-satellite scenarios. Today we mostly rely on “System 2” models — powerful but slow and heavy at inference — from our partners. “System 1” models (fast, intuitive) are coming back strongly and could add value not only on reactivity, but also on performance and ease of use. • Define benchmark scenarios of increasing complexity with the team: a single-satellite reactive loop, then a two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue loop, and, as a stretch goal, a multi-satellite scenario.
• Set the latency budget, accuracy needs, and execution context for each scenario.
• Build datasets and evaluation sets from Loft data, partner outputs, and open datasets.
